## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.8 — LAN access actually works now

> **Alpha**, but this one fixes two bugs that made the headline features of
> alpha.2 and alpha.6 unusable in practice. If you tried either, retry with
> this build.

Both were found by opening the UI on a real device on the LAN — an Android 6
photo frame — rather than testing loopback from the same machine. Neither is
visible that way.

### A wildcard bind rejected every WebSocket

With `listen.host` set to `0.0.0.0` — the normal way to expose HueMux on a
network — **every** WebSocket upgrade was rejected. The origin check compared
the browser's `Origin` against the configured host, but a browser connects to
a *concrete* address, so its origin is `192.168.1.x` and can never equal
`0.0.0.0`.

Static assets kept loading, because only `/ws` checks origin. So the page
rendered its header and then sat permanently empty, with nothing on screen to
explain it.

Wildcard binds now also accept an origin naming an address the machine
actually holds. Still not a wildcard — the same bounded set the self-signed
certificate is issued for.

### `--profile=lights` claimed it was unpaired, forever

The status pushed to the browser inferred "paired" from whether a screen-sync
engine existed. A lights-only profile has no engine *by design*, so a fully
paired, working server reported `paired: false` several times a second and the
UI showed a pairing panel it could never get past — while `/api/lights` was
returning real data the whole time.

**The lights profile has been unusable in a browser since
[alpha.2](https://github.com/zamber/huemux/releases/tag/v0.0.2-alpha.2).**
Loopback testing never caught it because the default profile has an engine.

### Old Android as a wall panel

Verified working on an Android 6.0.1 device via a modern browser: favorites,
entertainment-zone scenes with colour swatches, rooms, Polish translation, live
updates.

Note this is the **browser**, not the APK. Android 6's built-in WebView is
Chromium 44, which lacks CSS custom properties and Custom Elements v1 — the UI
uses 115 of the former and 2 of the latter, so it cannot render there. Any
Android device with a reasonably current browser can be a HueMux panel today
by pointing it at a LAN instance; the APK still targets arm64 and API 26.
